statement: You are given an n × m grid whose cells are 0 or 1, with at least one 1.

For every cell, find the distance to the nearest cell holding a 1. A step moves to a cell that shares an edge (up, down, left or right), so the distance between (i1, j1) and (i2, j2) is |i1 − i2| + |j1 − j2|. A cell that holds 1 is at distance 0.
Return an n × m grid in which each cell holds that distance.

examples.explanation: Every 0 here shares an edge with some 1, so every 0 gets distance 1 and every 1 stays 0.
There is one 1, in the centre, so each distance is the number of steps to the centre; the corners are 2 + 2 = 4 away.
